title: Demand and Attrition Rates for Allied Health Professionals
what_it_is: Demand and Attrition Rates for Allied Health Professionals

sections.label: AHP numbers and attrition
sections.summary: Registered allied health professionals rose from about 6,000 in 2019 to 7,500 in 2023, with public sector attrition up and community care attrition down.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: The total number of registered diagnostic radiographers, occupational therapists, physiotherapists, radiation therapists and speech therapists increased by 25%, from about 6,000 in 2019 to 7,500 in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Overall, the attrition of AHPs in the public healthcare sector increased slightly from 8.9% in 2018 to 11.6% in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: In the community care sector, the attrition of AHPs has fallen from 17.7% in 2018 to 11.3% in 2022.

sections.label: AHP attrition versus doctors nurses
sections.summary: Attrition rates for allied health professionals are higher than those for doctors and nurses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Indeed, the attrition rates for the AHPs are higher than that for the doctors and nurses.

sections.label: Doubled AHP course intakes
sections.summary: Over the last 10 years, intakes for allied health professional courses doubled from around 270 to 500.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Over the last 10 years, we have doubled intakes for AHP courses from around 270 to 500.

sections.label: Community care salary enhancements
sections.summary: Since 2011, salary enhancements in the community care sector, including for allied health professionals, have been supported.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: As I mentioned earlier, since 2011, we have been supporting salary enhancements in the community care sector, including for AHPs.

sections.label: Engagements on enhancing AHP profession
sections.summary: Engagements with allied health professionals are ongoing, and the suggestion to deep dive into enhancing the profession will be taken back for review.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Indeed, I think it is a good suggestion for us to deep dive and look as to how we can enhance these specific domains within that sector.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: So, definitely, as I mentioned earlier, we have already been in engagements with the AHPs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: So, this suggestion that is raised will be something that we can take back and look at, and see how we can enhance that profession, while improving the services to the people as well as enhancing the stature of the profession within the community.

sections.label: No private sector salary guidelines
sections.summary: There are currently no plans to develop salary guidelines for the private sector, general practitioner and specialist clinics.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Before I come Senior Parliamentary Secretary Rahayu, I remind Members to seek clarifications and not make speeches here.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: We do not have any plans currently to develop salary guidelines for the private sector, the general practitioner and specialist clinics at this juncture.

sections.label: Lower-income sector review consideration
sections.summary: The Member likely referred to lower-income people in that sector, and the speaker will take this back to consider a possible future review.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: But I note that the Member was probably referring to those who are in the lower-income bracket within that sector.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: I will have to take this back and then, we will see and consider whether this is something that we would need to review and look at in the future.
